lines.text: The monsoon comes to Mumbai late at night,
and every window keeps a square of light.
My mother sets a bucket by the stair,
my father talks to God about a chair.
The silver water sings along the street,
and slips inside the shoes of tired feet.
We do not sleep. We are too busy listening.
But somewhere in the dark the city turns,
and every child who fell asleep returns.
The roof still leaks. My father still says soon.
We sleep beneath the bucket and the moon.
